messages:
Marta Ruiz: Quick check — compact form on the new Console settings: do we go inline errors or a single toast at the top for validation failures? Context: many fields, tight vertical space, need strong a11y signal.
Devin Chen: my gut: inline for field-level stuff, toast for global failures (submission blocked). Inline = immediate mapping to the input.
Jamal Patel: agree re mapping, but inline eats vertical space. In compact mode we risk layout shift.
Ellie Wong: +1 to Jamal. Also concerned about screen reader announce order when inline error appears below a collapsed section.
Marta Ruiz: good call. If we do inline, we need a consistent affordance that doesn't push everything. maybe small icon + concise text, expand on focus?
Devin Chen: could do a truncated inline line like: "Required" or "Invalid email" and then reveal full helper when the field receives focus. keeps density.
Jamal Patel: worried about discoverability for keyboard users if error text is hidden until focus. Screen readers might miss it.
Ellie Wong: accessibility nit: use aria-invalid="true" on invalid inputs and aria-describedby pointing to the error id. That allows SR to read it even if visual helper is collapsed.
Marta Ruiz: ok so: visual compact inline that doesn't reflow, plus proper ARIA so SRs get full message. sounds promising. any copy preferences for required fields? asterisk vs explicit "Required" label?
Devin Chen: asterisk alone is ambiguous. I vote explicit inline "Required" at least for first field in a group, and a global legend that explains the asterisk.
Jamal Patel: contrast wise, small asterisks fail with the dim theme. If we keep the asterisk we must ensure WCAG contrast and tooltips on hover/focus.
Ellie Wong: also consider programmatic identification: add data-required="true" so automation/tests can assert presence.
Marta Ruiz: action item: design to propose two variants — (A) compact inline terse labels + aria-describedby + visibly persistent asterisk with high contrast, (B) no asterisk, inline "Required" copy. We should usability-test.
Devin Chen: another related: destructive actions in the same flow (delete pool). Do we use typed-confirmation or a more subtle confirm + undo toast?
Jamal Patel: for destructive ops I prefer typed-confirm on very destructive, irreversible actions. For minor deletes (single item) maybe confirm modal + undo toast.
Ellie Wong: Agree. Also copy: typed-confirmation should restate consequences in simple sentence and the exact token to type should be a single word, lowercase, no punctuation. Avoid ambiguity.
Marta Ruiz: example copy suggestion: "Type DELETE to permanently remove this pool. This action cannot be undone." Short, clear.
Devin Chen: add microcopy for autosave: "Changes saved" vs toast could clash with validation toasts. We should avoid overlapping toasts.
Jamal Patel: yep — recommendation: only one toast at a time, toasts queue or stack with clear priority (errors > undo > info). design-bot: filing a follow-up? :robot_face:
design-bot: Filed: https://go.redwood/design/issues/CI-427 — "Compact forms: inline vs toast validation + a11y checklist". Assigned to @Marta.
Ellie Wong: tiny CSS nit from QA: focus ring for compact inputs needs 3px min for visibility on low-contrast themes.
Marta Ruiz: noted. I'll mock both variants and include ARIA annotations and typed-confirm copy. I'll also add a small test matrix for SR announcement order and keyboard-only flows.
Devin Chen: thanks — can you add a fallback when aria-describedby target is offscreen (collapsed panels)? maybe move focus to the first invalid field on submit.
Marta Ruiz: yes — on submit we shift focus to the first invalid field and open the collapsed section containing it. that plus aria-described by should cover the SR flow.
Jamal Patel: thanks team — sounds like consensus. Quick PR review once mocks are up. :thumbsup:
Ellie Wong: +1 — will review a11y checklist.
Marta Ruiz: closing loop here, will share mock by EOD tomorrow.
